thread.title: Silicon Valley stocks rise slightly as Apple, Facebook gain

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Silicon Valley stocks rise slightly as Apple, Facebook gain

organizations.name: bloomberg silicon valley high tech index

text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 22, 2018, 1:50pm PST Updated Feb 22, 2018, 2:14pm PST An index of Silicon Valley's largest tech stocks gained slightly on Thursday, buoyed by a handful of strong performers. The Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Tech Index climbed 0.35 percent as seven of its 13 members posted gains. HP Inc. (NYSE: HPQ) was the index's top performer, gaining 1.04 percent in regular trading. Shares jumped further after-hours on strong earnings. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) climbed 1.02 percent, followed by Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), up 0.89 percent. Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) bounced up 0.61 percent. On the other side, Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO) fell 0.85 percent to lead the index's worst performers. eBay (NASDAQ: EBAY) slipped 0.67 percent and Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) dipped 0.35 percent. Among all Silicon Valley stocks, the best performers on Thursday: Mellanox Technologies, Ltd. (NASDAQ: MLNX), an Israeli-American supplier of computer networking products with offices in Sunnyvale, soared 11.28 percent after the company hiked its first-quarter revenue outlook. The company now expects quarterly revenue to come in between $240 million and $250 million, versus the $222 million to $232 million range it gave earlier. Mellanox also said that Chief Financial Officer Jacob Shulman will step down on May 4 to take an executive position at a "pre-IPO" company and that it's currently looking for his replacement. Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) gained 3.86 percent. Align Technology (NASDAQ: ALGN) climbed 2.99 percent. Arista Networks (NYSE: ANET) closed up 2.79 percent. VMware (NASDAQ: VMW) rose 1.86 percent. The worst performers among all Silicon Valley stocks: Roku (NASDAQ: ROKU) shares plummeted more than 17 percent after the Los Gatos-based TV tech company gave a weak quarterly earnings outlook. Synopsys (NASDAQ: SNPS) dropped 4.61 percent after reporting first-quarter earnings on Wednesday. SVB Financial Group (NASDAQ: SIVB), parent of Silicon Valley Bank, fell 3.46 percent. SunPower Corp. (NASDAQ: SPWR) fell 3.26 percent in regular trading — then recovered and made up those losses after-hours. The San Jose-based solar panel maker's shares have been rattled by President Trump's planned solar tariffs. GoPro (NASDAQ: GPRO) slipped 1.62 percent. – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 22, 2018, 1:50pm PST Updated Feb 22, 2018, 2:14pm PST Related Content
